Cross-fitted inputs for the distribution-function scan

Source: R/scan_cdf.R
crossfit_cdf.Rd

Splits the rows into folds and predicts, for each fold from models fitted on the other folds, \(\hat\eta_t(x) = P(Y \le t \mid R = 1, X = x)\) at every value of t, by a classification of \(Z = 1(Y \le t)\) among the observed rows, and \(\hat r\), as sharp_scan_cdf() requires. The learner is yours: fit_eta(train, newdata) receives the observed rows of the training folds with a 0/1 column z added and returns probabilities for newdata; it is called once per fold and value of t. Where all training rows share one value of z (a t below or above the observed outcomes), the prediction is that value and fit_eta is not called.

Usage

crossfit_cdf(
  data,
  response,
  outcome,
  t,
  fit_eta,
  fit_r,
  folds = 5L,
  seed = NULL,
  clip = 1e-06
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with all rows, observed and unobserved.

response

Name of the 0/1 response column.

outcome

Name of the outcome column.

t

Increasing grid of values.

fit_eta, fit_r

Functions (train, newdata) returning probabilities.

folds

Number of folds. Default 5.

seed

Optional seed for the fold assignment.

clip

Bound for \(\hat r\) and \(\hat\eta_t\), as in crossfit_inputs().

Value

A list with eta_t (an \(n \times T\) matrix), r, fold and t.

See also

sharp_scan_cdf(), crossfit_inputs()
